LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided Writing (1 lesson) • Chinese tones • Chinese characters: stro
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing, part of Writing 3.1 Guided Writing (1 lesson) • Chinese tones • Chinese characters: stro in Grade 4 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to learn Chinese characters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a recording related to nuclear family members and write them down in pinyin,

2. fill in the missing titles of nuclear family members in the family tree provided,

3. collaboratively join Chinese strokes to form characters on family and display them for peer mentorship,

4. compose simple sentences about nuclear family members using “这是......”(e.g. 这 是我 妈妈。),

5. work with peers to arrange sentence strips containing acquired vocabulary to create coherent sentences,

6. compare and contrast the use of pinyin and characters with their own writing system (i.e. 爸爸,妈妈 with baba, mama in Kiswahili respectively).

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a recording related to nuclear family members and write them down in pinyin,
2. fill in the missing titles of nuclear family members in the family tree provided,
3. collaboratively join Chinese strokes to form characters on family and display them for peer mentorship,
4. compose simple sentences about nuclear family members using “这是......”(e.g. 这 是我 妈妈。),
5. work with peers to arrange sentence strips containing acquired vocabulary to create coherent sentences,
6. compare and contrast the use of pinyin and characters with their own writing system (i.e. 爸爸,妈妈 with baba, mama in Kiswahili respectively).

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: The learner writes clearly and spells words correctly as they fill in the missing titles of

nuclear family members in the family tree correctly.

Values:
Responsibility: This is developed as the learner collaborates with others to arrange strips with vocabulary in the right order to

form coherent sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Intercultural awareness: This is promoted as the learner appreciates and acknowledges the similarities and differences in their

own writing system and Chinese.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner links their learning to Kiswahili on the concept of duplication of syllables when writing titles of family members.
